newsitem.title: UK: Defence says Grobbelaar innocent of UK match fixing.
newsitem.headline: Defence says Grobbelaar innocent of UK match fixing.

text.p: Former Liverpool goalkeeper Bruce Grobbelaar should be found not guilty of match fixing because the main prosecution witness in the case is a treacherous liar, the soccer star's lawyer said on Wednesday.
Rodney Klevan told a court that Chris Vincent, a former business partner of Grobbelaar, had no credibility and wanted to make as much money as he could from the case.
"Vincent is a liar without equal whose evidence must be totally rejected. He is a man who has corrupted this trial from beginning to end," Klevan said.
"This case is about heroes and a villain."

The case against Grobbelaar is based on secretly taped conversations in which he appeared to admit to Vincent that he had received large amounts of money for throwing matches on behalf of an Asian betting syndicate.
Grobbelaar could also be seen accepting a package of money which Vincent had offered him as part payment for throwing games for a second fictional syndicate.
But Klevan said Grobbelaar had concocted the stories of match-fixing in a bid to discover who Vincent was working for.
"Nothing that was said was meant to be a truthful admission of his conduct," said Klevan, admitting that his client had been foolish.
"He appreciates it should have been done in a different way. Any talk of throwing games is stupid and dangerous and that is why he is here today," he said.
Grobbelaar is accused with former Wimbledon keeper Hans Segers, ex-Wimbledon and Aston Villa striker John Fashanu and Malaysian businessman Heng Suan Lim of rigging games.

Both goalkeepers admit receiving money from Lim to forecast the results of games but all four men deny rigging matches. The judge is due to sum the case up on Thursday and Friday before the jury starts deliberating on Monday.

Vincent, who fell out with Grobbelaar after the collapse of a Zimbabwean safari park venture in July 1994, told the court last month he wanted to bring down the keeper while making as much money as possible.
Grobbelaar, who lost 60,000 pounds ($98,210) in the venture, said he had pulled the plug when he learned much of the money had vanished and Vincent could not supply an explanation.

"Vincent is a repository of treachery. He is a serpent. No creator of literature could have invented him. He doesn't care for truth or justice. He cares only for two things -- himself and money," Klevan said.
Witness after witness had portrayed Grobbelaar as a widely respected man who willingly donated his time and money to worthy causes, he said.
"All the evidence apart from Vincent's is of a generous open-handed, open-hearted man, a giver not a taker, a man of a lifetime's achievement."
A series of former players also appeared in court to say Grobbelaar had always been a consummate player and had never shown signs of throwing games.
"These are the crucial professionals. If they don't see anything untoward, nothing untoward occurred," Klevan said.
The prosecution alleges that Grobbelaar received 40,000 pounds for throwing a match against Newcastle in November 1993 and tried to fix the results of four other games.
Klevan focussed on Vincent's character, saying he had been involved in a string of failed business ventures before he met Grobbelaar in 1992 but had not told the keeper of his past.
"The crown (prosecution) know he is tarnished beyond measure but they want you to rely on him because it suits them," he said. ($1=.6109 Pound)
